First, I need to understand what it means to "steal" the basketball in this context. From what I know, in basketball, stealing the ball refers to a defensive player taking possession of the ball from an offensive player. This is a common and accepted part of the game. Now, if someone is playing on the offensive side, it's reasonable to expect that the defensive team will try to prevent them from scoring, which includes trying to steal the ball. It's part of the game's strategy and rules. So, expecting the other team to try to steal the ball seems to be a realistic expectation based on how basketball is played. But then, is it right or wrong to have this expectation? Well, if we're talking about the rules of the game, it's perfectly acceptable and even expected for defensive players to try to steal the ball. It's part of the competition. However, if the expectation is that the other team should not try to steal the ball, that would be against the rules and the spirit of the game. So, in this scenario, expecting the other team to try to steal the ball is not only right but also a fundamental aspect of playing basketball. It's part of what makes the game challenging and competitive. If the other team didn't try to steal the ball, it would be unusual and perhaps even unfair to the offensive team. Moreover, in a fair and competitive game, both teams should have the opportunity to score and defend. Expecting the other team to try to steal the ball maintains this balance and ensures that the game remains competitive and exciting for both players and spectators. In summary, expecting the other team to try to steal the basketball is right because it aligns with the rules and strategies of the game, promoting fairness and competition.
